questions.question: In which organelle does cellular respiration take place?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion releases energy from glucose and is called the powerhouse of the cell.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Photosynthesis takes place in the
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps the light energy used to make food.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The cell wall of a plant cell is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Cellulose fibres give the plant cell wall its rigidity.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The function of the ribosome in a cell is
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Meiosis differs from mitosis in that meiosis
options: halves the chromosome number of the daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis is reduction division, producing haploid gametes from a diploid cell.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human body cell?
questions.explanation: Body cells are diploid with 23 pairs, giving 46 chromosomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The raw materials required for photosynthesis are
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide and water are combined using light energy trapped by chlorophyll.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The products of photosynthesis are
questions.explanation: Glucose is the food made, and oxygen is released as a by-product.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which reagent is used to test for the presence of starch in a leaf?
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black in the presence of starch.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The enzyme in saliva that acts on starch is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) breaks starch down to maltose.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pepsin is most active in
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach provides the low pH that pepsin requires.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the
questions.explanation: Bile is concentrated in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum to emulsify fats.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Absorption of digested food takes place mainly in the
questions.explanation: The villi of the small intestine give a very large surface area for absorption.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Oxygen is transported in the blood by
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which blood component is essential for clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets trigger the cascade that converts fibrinogen to fibrin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which chamber of the mammalian heart has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.explanation: It pumps blood to the whole body, so it must generate the highest pressure.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Arteries differ from veins in that arteries
options: carry blood away from the heart
questions.explanation: Direction of flow is the reliable distinction; the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Water and mineral salts are transported in flowering plants through the
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels carry water upwards; phloem carries manufactured food.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called
questions.explanation: Most of it occurs through the stomata of the leaves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The products of aerobic respiration in animals are
questions.explanation: Glucose is completely oxidised, releasing the maximum energy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Anaerobic respiration in human muscle produces
questions.explanation: Lactic acid accumulates during vigorous exercise, causing muscle fatigue.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The energy currency of the cell is
questions.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate releases energy when its terminal phosphate bond is broken.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each nephron filters blood and reabsorbs useful substances.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which organ excretes excess water and salts in the form of sweat?
questions.explanation: Sweat glands in the skin excrete water, salts and a little urea.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The lungs excrete
questions.explanation: Both are waste products of respiration removed during exhalation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Support in young herbaceous plants is largely provided by
questions.explanation: Turgid cells press against their walls and hold the plant upright; wilting follows water loss.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The joint at the elbow is an example of a
questions.explanation: A hinge joint permits movement in one plane only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The biceps and triceps of the upper arm are described as
questions.explanation: One contracts while the other relaxes, producing opposite movements.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
questions.explanation: A neurone conducts impulses; a synapse is the junction between two of them.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which part of the brain is responsible for balance and the coordination of muscular activity?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum fine-tunes posture and movement.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Insulin, the hormone that lowers blood glucose level, is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Adrenaline is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys and prepare the body for emergency action.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The growth of a plant shoot towards a source of light is called
questions.explanation: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, making those cells elongate and the shoot bend towards light.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In dim light, vision depends mainly on the
questions.explanation: Rods are sensitive to low light intensity but do not distinguish colour.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma is called
questions.explanation: Fertilisation follows pollination, when the male nucleus fuses with the ovule.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Pollen grains are produced in the
questions.explanation: The anther is the pollen-bearing part of the stamen.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The sperm meets the egg in the fallopian tube (oviduct), and the embryo then implants in the uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The main function of the placenta is to
options: allow exchange of materials between mother and foetus
protect the foetus from physical shock
questions.explanation: Oxygen and nutrients pass to the foetus and wastes pass back, without the blood mixing.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt) gives a phenotypic ratio of
questions.explanation: The offspring are TT, Tt, Tt and tt, so three show the dominant tall phenotype.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The observable characteristic of an organism is its
questions.explanation: The genotype is the genetic make-up; the phenotype is how it is expressed.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In humans, the sex chromosomes of a normal male are
questions.explanation: The father's sperm carries either X or Y, so it determines the sex of the child.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia in humans is caused by
options: a deficiency of iron in the diet
questions.explanation: An altered gene produces abnormal haemoglobin, distorting the red blood cells.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Natural selection as the mechanism of evolution was proposed by
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed the inheritance of acquired characteristics, which is not accepted today.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In a food chain, green plants are referred to as
questions.explanation: They manufacture their own food by photosynthesis and begin every food chain.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: As one moves up successive trophic levels in an ecosystem, the available energy
questions.explanation: Energy is lost as heat and in respiration at each transfer, so less is passed on.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: All the organisms of the same species living together in a given area constitute a
questions.explanation: Several populations of different species together form a community.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Nitrogen fixation in the root nodules of leguminous plants is carried out by
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Plants that are structurally adapted to survive in very dry habitats are called
questions.explanation: Xerophytes reduce water loss with thick cuticles, sunken stomata and reduced leaves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The system of naming organisms using two names, the genus and the species, is called
questions.explanation: For example Homo sapiens, in which the genus is written first and capitalised.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is the most immediate consequence of deforestation?
questions.explanation: Removing the plant cover exposes bare soil to the direct action of rain and wind.
questions.subject: Biology
